banned_anti_patterns.description: Raw PII (email, phone, IP) in metric/trace labels; violates cardinality bounds and leaks sensitive data in logs/dashboards.
Plaintext tier_direct PII stored in database or cache; violates encryption rule (PII-1-RULE-001).
Treating client-provided PII or consent state as authoritative; server MUST re-validate and re-encrypt on every write.
Application-level tenant filtering instead of PostgreSQL RLS; enables cross-tenant data leakage via SQL injection or logic bugs.
Retaining tier_direct PII beyond DATA-1 baseline (90 days operational) without explicit legal justification and audit trail.
Using raw device_id or IP address for cross-session user tracking without consent; violates GDPR legitimate interest test.
Aggregating PII across tenants (org_id) without explicit superadmin authorization; enables cross-org profiling.

changes: Split subject_key semantics: subject_key is now an opaque UUIDv7 issued by PII-1 and MUST NOT be derived from direct or quasi identifiers.
Added subject_lookup_key_hash as a vault-only deterministic HMAC-SHA256 lookup/upsert key that MUST NOT be emitted outside PII-1.
Clarified that PII-1 remains a non-producer contract: PII writes append-only audit records; DSAR-1 owns formal DSAR lifecycle/outbox events.
Removed orphaned EVT-1 dependency floor from PII-1 because PII-1 remains non-producer.
Normalized PII capability names to dot-scoped names pending IAM-1 alignment.
Banned subject_key and subject_lookup_key_hash from metrics, traces, logs, analytics dimensions, vendor payloads, COMM/NOTIF/TRK/BI/API payloads, and external API payloads.
Lock subject_key as generated UUIDv7 (NOT derived from direct PII) to enforce vault exclusivity and org-scoped DSAR.
Clarify encryption hierarchy: per-subject envelope keys wrapped by per-org tenant KMS key; DSAR cryptoshred destroys envelope keys.
Align DSAR capability references with IAM-1.
Lock joinable identifiers as pseudonymous PII to prevent re-identification via join keys in exports/BI/telemetry.
Add PII->DATA-1 classification interop mapping (c0..c4) and export ceiling rules.
Expand PII field registry with common joinable identifiers.
Align dependency minimum versions to current suite baseline where known.

dependencies.reason: Blueprint baseline patterns and anti-pattern bans.
Suite schema source of truth for contract-suite/1.0, test-gates/1.0, bundle-manifest/1.0.
Test-gates schema + authoring constraints for CI strict.
Constitutional invariants: immutability boundaries, truth preservation, and platform-wide constraints.
Multi-tenancy: org_id sealing, hide-existence semantics, and cross-tenant prohibition.
Capability-based authorization model for PII access, export, and break-glass. (includes DSAR/PII capabilities and support roles).
Encryption/key management expectations required for PII vault and cryptoshred semantics.
Classification tiers + minimization/redaction posture; retention class mapping.
Retention, archival, and destruction semantics; DSAR execution evidence expectations.
Consent categories and withdrawal semantics that constrain identity mapping/linking.
Tracking schema and payload constraints: PII-1 imposes hard MUST NOT rules on TRK events.
Immutable ledger boundary: cryptoshred MUST NOT mutate postings or financial truth.
Immutable order truth boundary: snapshots MUST NOT be mutated by DSAR/consent actions.
Immutable price snapshot boundary: cryptoshred MUST NOT alter historical pricing truth.
PII access anomaly monitoring expectations; detection and evidence posture.
Canonical error envelope and subcode conventions for privacy/PII errors.
Enforce anti-differencing controls for aggregate analytics surfaces (query normalization, caching windows, and rate limiting).

complementary_suppression.rule: When any cell in a breakdown is suppressed due to min_population_size, the system MUST suppress at least one additional cell to prevent reconstruction by subtraction.

anonymization_threshold.notes: This rule prevents singling-out / inference re-identification in pseudonymous analytics.
anonymization_threshold.statement: Aggregated analytics outputs SHALL NOT be displayed when underlying population size is less than min_population_size unless access is capability-gated as PII export.

totals_handling.rule: Totals MUST NOT enable reconstruction of suppressed cells.

anti_differencing_controls.evidence: Audit logs MUST record canonical_query_key, time_bucket, cache_hit, suppression_applied, and override_used.
anti_differencing_controls.purpose: Prevent re-identification via differencing attacks against anonymized/aggregate analytics.
requirements: Analytics query surfaces SHALL enforce query_normalization so semantically-equivalent queries map to a canonical cache key.
Analytics query surfaces SHALL enforce minimum_time_bucket='day' for time-series breakdowns.
Analytics query surfaces SHALL enforce cache_window_seconds=86400 for aggregate query results (>=1 day).
Analytics query surfaces SHALL enforce per_actor_rate_limits: max_total_queries_per_hour=120 and max_distinct_queries_per_hour=30 per actor per org_id.
Any override of suppression or bucket controls MUST be export-only (no UI display) and MUST require pii.export capability with mandatory audit reason.

consent_interaction.consent_does_not_override_retention: Consent withdrawal does NOT extend retention beyond DATA-1 baseline (90 days operational); PII deleted at earlier of (consent_withdrawal + 30d, retention_expiry)
consent_interaction.consent_proof_integrity: Consent records are append-only per ARCH-1; DSAR deletion MUST NOT mutate consent_records table; consent metadata preserved for audit
consent_interaction.consent_withdrawal_to_deletion: When consent withdrawn for purpose X, raw PII used exclusively for purpose X MUST be scheduled for DSAR deletion within 30 days unless legal retention exception applies (LED-1, ORD-1)
consent_interaction.description: Integration with CONSENT-1 for consent-driven PII lifecycle

requirements: Operation MUST require IAM capability dsar.process (or dsar.export/dsar.cryptoshred depending on action).
Operation MUST record audit entry with bounded reason code dsar_legal_obligation and evidence refs (non-PII).
dsar_legal_obligation_override.statement: Consent state MUST NOT gate DSAR operations; DSAR lawful basis is legal obligation.

consent_interaction.most_restrictive_wins: If user privacy_mode is 'eu_strict', PII collection MUST be minimized even if consent granted; collect only fields required for transactional necessity

cryptoshred.definition: Cryptoshred SHALL destroy the cryptographic material and mapping records required to link subject_key to any real-world identity, without mutating immutable facts.

deletion_workflow.authorization: IAM-1 actor with DSAR permission or superadmin
deletion_workflow.deletion_method: Cryptoshred: destroy the subject identity mapping keys and any PII field-level envelope keys, rendering vault ciphertext permanently unlinkable; schedule purge of redundant ciphertext blobs per ARCH-1/DATA-1.
deletion_workflow.description: GDPR Article 17 / POPIA Section 24: Right to erasure
deletion_workflow.error_handling: ERR-PII-007 if subject not found (hide-existence); ERR-PII-010 if timeline breached
exceptions: Audit trail metadata (who/when/why but not PII content)
deletion_workflow.ledger_preservation: DSAR deletion MUST NOT mutate LED-1 postings; financial records remain immutable per ARCH-1
deletion_workflow.recovery: No recovery after cryptoshred execution; DSAR cancellation is only allowed before execution completes.
deletion_workflow.scope: Single org_id only; cascade to all PII records but preserve audit trail metadata
deletion_workflow.telemetry_handling: TRK-1 raw behavioral events tied to subject_key/session_key SHALL be deleted OR transformed to anonymous (no subject_key/session_key) while preserving only aggregate analytics subjectless outputs.

dsar_audit_trail.description: PII-1 does not produce formal DSAR lifecycle/outbox events. PII-1 writes append-only vault audit records consumed by DSAR-1. DSAR-1 owns DSAR requested/completed/failed lifecycle events and EVT registry integration.
dsar_audit_trail.retention: 7 years minimum for regulatory audit via ARCH-1/DATA-1

export_workflow.authorization: IAM-1 actor with DSAR permission or superadmin
export_workflow.description: GDPR Article 15 / POPIA Section 23: Data subject access request
export_workflow.error_handling: ERR-DSAR-TIMEOUT if export takes >30 days; ERR-PII-006 if cross-tenant access attempted
excluded_data: Other users' data in same org
export_workflow.scope: Single org_id only; no cross-tenant data leakage

portability_workflow.authorization: IAM-1 actor with DSAR permission or superadmin
portability_workflow.description: GDPR Article 20: Right to data portability
portability_workflow.scope: User-provided data only (name, email, phone, consent records); excludes derived analytics or inferred data

observability_cardinality_rules.description: Prevents PII leakage via high-cardinality metric labels and trace attributes

no_raw_pii_in_labels.cardinality_limit: Subject-level identifiers are forbidden regardless of cardinality; allowed labels must remain operational and non-subject.
no_raw_pii_in_labels.enforcement_mechanism: OBS-1 metric aggregation MUST reject labels not in allowed_labels list; runtime validation required

trace_attributes.sampling: Parent-based head sampling; PII-heavy traces MUST be tail-sampled at ≤1% if org_id cardinality >1000

subject_identifier_observability_ban.statement: subject_key and subject_lookup_key_hash MUST NOT appear in metric labels, trace attributes, log fields, analytics dimensions, BI dimensions, vendor payloads, COMM/NOTIF/TRK/BI/API payloads, or external API payloads.

classes.description: Direct identifiers that can identify a natural person without additional data (or with minimal effort).
Special category or highly sensitive personal data; handling requires explicit consent category and additional controls.
Identifiers that do not directly identify a person but can be linked back through controlled mappings.
Data that cannot reasonably be linked to a person by the platform after enforced minimization and thresholding.
Aggregated statistics computed over populations where singling-out is prevented by thresholding and bucketing.

tier_direct.description: Directly identifies an individual (name, email, phone, national ID, biometric data).
tier_direct.retention_policy: 90 days operational baseline per DATA-1; archive post-90d with continued encryption; delete on DSAR or 7-year maximum.
tier_direct.storage_policy: AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest with KMS-managed per-tenant keys; quarterly key rotation mandatory.
tier_direct.transmission_policy: TLS 1.2+ only; no plaintext logging; hash with SHA-256 if logging required for debugging.

tier_non_identifying.description: Aggregated or anonymized data that cannot re-identify individuals (aggregate counts, percentile distributions).
tier_non_identifying.retention_policy: Indefinite retention permitted; no DSAR deletion obligation.
tier_non_identifying.storage_policy: No encryption required; plaintext storage permitted.
tier_non_identifying.transmission_policy: Standard HTTPS; permitted in public analytics and reporting.

tier_pseudonymous.description: Stable pseudonymous identifier issued by the PII boundary (subject_key uuid_v7, session_key UUIDv7). Not derived from direct identifiers.
tier_pseudonymous.retention_policy: Subject keys: 7 years for audit trail; session keys: 90 days operational.
tier_pseudonymous.storage_policy: Plaintext storage permitted only inside approved domain/vault records where needed for joins; subject_key immutable after issuance within org_id; session_key ephemeral; subject_lookup_key_hash is vault-only.
tier_pseudonymous.transmission_policy: TLS 1.2+ inside authorized service boundaries only; subject_key MUST NOT be used in telemetry/observability labels, traces, logs, analytics dimensions, vendor payloads, or external API payloads.

tier_quasi_id.description: Can identify individual when combined with other data (IP address, user agent, postal code, age bucket, device ID).
tier_quasi_id.retention_policy: Hashed values: 90 days operational; raw values: never persisted beyond request lifecycle.
tier_quasi_id.storage_policy: Hashed with daily-rotated salt from KMS; raw value NOT persisted; hash algorithm SHA-256 or BLAKE3.
tier_quasi_id.transmission_policy: TLS 1.2+; hashed value only in logs and telemetry; raw value ephemeral (request-scoped only).

export_ceiling_rules.statement: Any export payload containing any field classified as pii_direct or pseudonymous MUST be treated as at least DATA-1 class c3 (restricted_pii).
Any export payload containing any field classified as pii_sensitive MUST be treated as DATA-1 class c4 (regulated_high_risk).
Exports treated as DATA-1 class c2 or lower MUST NOT contain joinable identifiers (per joinable_identifier_policy) and MUST NOT contain any direct identifiers.

pii_class_to_data_class_default.rationale: Joinable identifiers enable re-identification through controlled mappings.
Special-category or regulated personal data is high-risk.
Aggregates can be confidential; anti-differencing controls apply.

pii_classification_taxonomy.description: Four-tier classification system for personal data fields with mandatory storage, transmission, and retention policies per GDPR/POPIA standards.

joinable_identifier_policy.classification_rule: If a field_id matches explicit_field_ids or any field_id_patterns and is not in exempt_field_ids, it MUST be classified at least as pseudonymous.
joinable_identifier_policy.definition: A joinable identifier is any identifier that can be used (directly or via stable joins) to resolve, infer, or retrieve a natural person within the platform boundary (including via orders, memberships, attendees, or identity mappings).
notes: Conservative by design: treat join keys as PII for exports even when they are not direct identifiers.
Exemptions cover non-person entity identifiers that are not resolvable to a natural person without additional data.

hashed_quasi_id_derivation.retention: Hashed value: 90 days operational; raw value: never persisted beyond request scope
hashed_quasi_id_derivation.salt_source: KMS-managed daily salt rotated at 00:00 UTC; per-tenant

session_key_derivation.notes: Session keys are NOT reversible to user identity; used for session tracking only
session_key_derivation.renewal: per-session; expires on logout or session timeout (24 hours max)

subject_key_derivation.input: PII-1 generated entropy and UUIDv7 timestamp component only; MUST NOT include email, phone, name, IP address, device id, order id, membership id, actor id, user id, provider id, tracking id, or any direct/quasi identifier
subject_key_derivation.tenant_scope: stable for the issued subject within org_id after creation
subject_key_derivation.exposure_rule: subject_key is a pseudonymous join identifier and MUST NOT be emitted to metrics, traces, logs, analytics dimensions, vendor payloads, COMM/NOTIF/TRK/BI/API payloads, or external API payloads

subject_lookup_key_hash_derivation.key: versioned secret pepper owned by SEC-1 and accessible only inside the PII vault boundary
subject_lookup_key_hash_derivation.output: vault-confined binary/hash value used only for deterministic lookup/upsert

invariants.statement: A tier_direct PII field MUST never be stored unencrypted at rest; encrypted_at_rest constraint is constitutional (cannot be waived).
An org_id value MUST be immutable once a PII record is created; no org_id modification allowed (TEN-1 invariant).
A query for PII MUST filter by org_id via PostgreSQL RLS; no application-only filtering is acceptable (security-by-database, not security-by-application).

subject_key MUST be an opaque UUIDv7 generated by PII-1 and MUST remain stable for the subject within org_id after issuance. subject_key MUST NOT be derived from direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, tracking identifiers, analytics identifiers, provider identifiers, or any deterministic hash of those identifiers. Deterministic re-identification or idempotent lookup MUST use a separate vault-confined subject_lookup_key_hash.
A DSAR request MUST be honored within 30 days; timeline breach is regulatory non-compliance (GDPR fines up to 4% global revenue).

A consent withdrawal or DSAR deletion MUST NOT mutate transactional truth (LED-1 ledger postings, ORD-1 price snapshots); consent and PII are metadata only, never authoritative for revenue recognition.
An encryption key rotation MUST be auditable; old keys MUST be retained for historical decryption; no key destruction without 7-year retention minimum and DPO approval.

Aggregated outputs (counts, averages, percentages, breakdowns) MUST NOT be displayed when the underlying population size is below the anonymization threshold (k=5) unless access is capability-gated as a PII export job with audit evidence.

Direct identifiers (pii_direct) MUST live only in the PII vault. Direct identifiers MUST NOT appear in tracking payloads, analytics read models, logs, immutable ledger postings, or order/price snapshots.

invariants.rationale: Privacy law obligations require DSAR fulfillment irrespective of marketing/analytics consent. Blocking DSAR on consent would create regulatory and operational risk.
invariants.scope: org_id scoped; platform-wide DSAR requires platform capability + explicit multi-org scope.
invariants.statement: DSAR processing (identity verification, export, and cryptoshred) SHALL NOT be blocked by consent state; DSAR operates under legal obligation and MUST be permitted only with explicit IAM capability and append-only audit evidence.

invariants.rule: Aggregate analytics MUST NOT display any cell with population count < 5 (min_population_size).
If any cell is suppressed for k-anonymity, complementary suppression MUST be applied to prevent reconstruction by differencing.
Time-series analytics MUST use minimum time bucket of day for breakdowns to reduce re-identification risk.
Aggregate analytics MUST implement query normalization, caching (>=86400s), and per-actor rate limits to reduce differencing attack surface.
A joinable identifier MUST be classified at least as pseudonymous PII and MUST be treated as DATA-1 class c3 (restricted_pii) for exports/BI/telemetry payload classification.
Any payload containing pii_sensitive fields MUST be classified as DATA-1 class c4 (regulated_high_risk) and MUST require regulated export capability + audit logging.

rules.description: All tier_direct PII MUST be encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; no plaintext storage permitted except for exceptions (org_id, record_id, timestamps, pseudonymous keys).
PII records MUST be tenant-sealed via org_id immutability and PostgreSQL RLS; no application-level tenant filtering permitted.
Cross-tenant PII access attempts MUST be rejected at database layer with ERR-NOT-FOUND (hide-existence per TEN-1); never ERR-FORBIDDEN which leaks existence.

Pseudonymized join identifiers exposed outside the vault MUST be opaque identifiers issued by PII-1. Deterministic lookup hashes MAY exist only inside the PII vault and MUST be HMAC-SHA256 based, tenant-bound, normalizer-versioned, secret-peppered, and never emitted outside PII-1.
Data subject rights (export, deletion, portability) MUST be executed within 30 days per GDPR Article 15-20 / POPIA Section 23-24; timeline breach is non-compliance.
Encryption keys MUST be rotated quarterly (every 90 days); old keys retained for decryption of historical records with 7-year retention minimum; key destruction requires DPO approval.

Raw PII and subject-level identifiers, including subject_key and subject_lookup_key_hash, MUST NOT appear in metric labels, trace attributes, log fields, analytics dimensions, vendor payloads, COMM/NOTIF/TRK/BI/API payloads, or external API payloads.

PII-1 MUST NOT emit formal domain outbox events. PII modifications, encryption operations, pseudonymization actions, and DSAR support actions MUST write append-only PII audit records; DSAR-1 owns formal DSAR lifecycle/outbox events.

storage_encryption_rules.emergency_key_access: Superadmin break-glass via GOV-0 with audit trail; requires justification and DPO notification

exceptions.reason: org_id and record_id required for RLS and indexing; timestamps required for retention queries; subject_key/session_key are pseudonymous but remain subject-level and are forbidden from observability, analytics, vendor, COMM/NOTIF/TRK/BI/API, and external API payloads. subject_lookup_key_hash is vault-only and is not a general storage exception.

storage_encryption_rules.key_derivation: KMS-managed per-tenant keys; key_id stored with record; key material NEVER persisted in application database
key_hierarchy: tenant_master_key (KMS, per org_id) wraps envelope keys
subject_envelope_key (DEK, per subject_key within org_id) encrypts tier_direct PII rows/columns

clarification: tenant_master_key rotation MAY retain historical keys for non-shredded subjects.
wrapped envelope keys for cryptoshredded subjects MUST be deleted; historical tenant keys MUST NOT resurrect access.

storage_encryption_rules.rotation_procedure: Generate new key_id from KMS; re-encrypt all tier_direct PII with new key; old keys retained for historical decryption with 7-year retention

tier_direct.cryptoshred: DSAR cryptoshred MUST destroy the subject_envelope_key (and wrapped key blob) for the subject_key; vault ciphertext MAY remain but MUST be irrecoverable without the destroyed key.
tier_direct.encryption_at_rest: MUST use subject_envelope_key (per subject_key within org_id); envelope key MUST be wrapped by tenant_master_key in KMS.
notes: This enables subject-level cryptoshred without destroying org-wide keys.
tenant_master_key rotation MUST NOT re-enable access to cryptoshredded subjects.
Telemetry/tracking events must never contain direct identifiers (e.g., email, phone, gov_id).
subject_key, subject_lookup_key_hash, and session_key MUST NOT be emitted to TRK-1 payloads, vendor payloads, logs, metrics, traces, BI dimensions, or external APIs.

trk1_alignment.description: TRK-1 integration rules for PII-safe telemetry
trk1_alignment.enforcement: TRK-1 event schema validation MUST reject payloads with forbidden fields; CI lint gate enforces schema compliance
trk1_alignment.no_raw_pii_rule: TRK-1 payloads MUST NOT include raw email, phone, IP address, full user_agent, name, or any tier_direct field
trk1_alignment.subject_key_standard: subject_key remains vault-issued and MUST NOT be emitted to TRK-1 payloads; use subjectless or aggregate telemetry only outside the PII vault.

subcodes.PII_ACCESS_DENIED: Actor lacks required IAM capability or tenant scope.
subcodes.PII_AUDIT_REASON_REQUIRED: Audit reason is required and MUST be from bounded list.
subcodes.PII_CRYPTOSHRED_FAILED: Cryptoshred operation failed; MUST preserve immutable truth and emit audit evidence.
subcodes.PII_DATA_CLASSIFICATION_VIOLATION: Data classification rules violated (storage, transmission, retention, or redaction).
subcodes.PII_EXPORT_TOKEN_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED: Export retrieval token invalid, expired, already used, or not found.
subcodes.PII_LOG_REDACTION_VIOLATION: Logs contain disallowed PII or failed deterministic redaction.
subcodes.PII_MAPPING_FORBIDDEN_BY_CONSENT: Identity mapping/linking is forbidden by consent or withdrawal.
subcodes.PII_VAULT_ALIAS_FORBIDDEN: Attempted to create/store alias outside PII vault or alias class forbidden.
subcodes.PII_VAULT_ALIAS_NOT_FOUND: Requested alias or mapping does not exist (hide-existence rules apply).

migration.compat_strategy: Semver only; policy version immutable per ARCH-1.
migration.data_backfills: If adding new PII field to field_registry, backfill with encrypted=false flag and schedule encryption job; do NOT block deployments on backfill.
migration.field_registry_immutability: Existing field classifications MUST NOT change tier retroactively; new fields require minor version bump.
migration.rolling_deploy_safety: Encryption and pseudonymization MUST remain idempotent across N and N-1 versions; key_id immutability ensures compatibility.

slo_targets.release_block: if p99 > 500ms for 5 min, page on-call

never_owns: Consent state machine or purpose grants (CONSENT-1)
out_of_scope: Legal interpretation of GDPR Article 17 or POPIA Section 24 (legal review required)
External DLP tooling or SIEM integration
owns: PII field classification taxonomy (direct, quasi-identifier, pseudonymous, non-identifying)
Storage encryption rules (AES-256-GCM, KMS key derivation, quarterly rotation)
Pseudonymization standards (opaque subject_key UUIDv7; vault-only subject_lookup_key_hash; session_key UUIDv7)
Data subject rights workflows (export, deletion, portability within 30 days)
PII-to-TRK-1 integration rules (no raw PII in telemetry payloads)
Observability cardinality rules (no raw PII in metric labels)
Tenant-sealed PII access control (org_id immutability, hide-existence semantics)

security_posture.notes: Tier_direct PII encrypted at rest; tier_quasi_id hashed only. All PII access requires org_id context and IAM-1 authorization.

summary: Normative authority for personal data classification (GDPR/POPIA), encryption at rest (AES-256-GCM), pseudonymization standards (uuid_v7 subject keys), tenant-sealed PII handling via org_id + PostgreSQL RLS, and data subject rights tooling (export, deletion, portability) within 30-day timelines. Enforces no-raw-PII-in-telemetry rule across TRK-1 and OBS-1 integrations.

tenancy.notes: Platform superadmin has platform-scoped PII viewing for compliance audits; organizers see only their org_id data. No application-level tenant filtering permitted; PostgreSQL RLS is constitutional requirement.
tenancy.superadmin_bypass: allowed via GOV-0 break-glass with audit trail

title: PII Boundary, Identity Mapping, and Cryptoshred Contract

approved_authority_corrections.ownership: PII-1 owns direct email/phone identifiers and tenant-bound PII evidence; subject_lookup_key_hash is vault-only and MUST NOT be exposed to IAM.
